page: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 1 dedicated vCPU, corresponding to 1 physical x86_64 core running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system includes 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistence, and there are no hardware accelerators or GPUs included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute output alongside predictable multi-core constraints due to its single vCPU design. The instance scored 3031.88 in single-core stress-ng tests and achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1955.0, placing it in the top 25% of single-threaded benchmarks. The AMD architecture includes modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and SHA-NI, which support modern cryptographic and algorithmic tasks. However, aggregate throughput is inherently limited by the single-core footprint, with multi-core Geekbench metrics (1956.0) and overall PassMark CPU scores (2667.55) placing in the lower percentiles.

Memory bandwidth shows balanced performance on write tests (26.46 GB/sec uncached), but uncached read bandwidth drops to 33.84 GB/sec. Redis SET operations measured 2.66 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 2.2 GB/sec. LLM inference on a lightweight 135M model reached 104.27 tokens per second for text generation.

Given its dedicated core and modern DDR5 memory architecture, the instance provides reliable baseline single-thread execution without CPU credit throttling. It represents a resource-efficient choice for lightweight workloads, background automation tasks, small microservices, development environments, and low-traffic web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is a general purpose instance powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processor using the Nitro hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical vCPU paired with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. It includes no bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores of 1955.0 and stress-ng single-core results ranking in the top 25%. However, overall system throughput is bounded by the single-core constraint, resulting in lower scores on parallelized benchmarks such as compilation and multi-core processing. With advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 variants, the instance provides steady, predictable processing capacity. Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is best fitted for low-concurrency web serving, small microservices, CI/CD utility steps, and development workloads that do not demand parallel processing.
